newsitem.title: UK: FTSE Intl, Athens Stock Exchange to launch index.
newsitem.headline: FTSE Intl, Athens Stock Exchange to launch index.

text.p: FTSE International, the company best known for managing the FTSE 100 index, on Tuesday said it was teaming up with the Athens Stock Exchange to publish an index based on the top 20 biggest and most liquid Greek stocks.
FTSE said the FTSE/ASE 20, as it will be known, is expected to be launched on September 24, 1997.
The new index would be calculated and published on a real-time basis by the Athens Stock Exchange and would run in parallel to the existing ASE General index.
The index constituents of the FTSE/ASE 20 would represent about 65 percent of the market capitalisation of the Greek stock market and would be reviewed half-yearly.
The index was designed to help derivatives trading on the Athens exchange for which plans are currently underway.
For the time being, the company predicted the new index would be used for performance measurement and as a basis for index-tracking funds.
The FTSE/ASE20 expands upon existing partnerships between FTSE International and European stock exchanges.
In partnership with the Amsterdam Stock Exchange, the company already calculates the FTSE Eurotop 300 index which is expected to go live in July this year.
FTSE said it was in dialogue with other overseas exchanges concerning joint projects to produce more indices but declined to elaborate.
